blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Abraham was old and well along in years, and his son Isaac still had no wife. So Abraham sent his oldest and most trusted servant all the way back to the old country, to his own people, to find a wife for his son.

verses.text: And the servant took ten camels of the camels of his master, and departed; for all the goods of his master were in his hand: and he arose, and went to Mesopotamia, unto the city of Nahor.

verses.text: And he made his camels to kneel down without the city by a well of water at the time of the evening, even the time that women go out to draw water.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Evening time. A long way from home. A strange town, a well, and ten thirsty camels. That servant did not know a soul there. So before he did anything else, he prayed.

verses.text: And he said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day, and shew kindness unto my master Abraham.

verses.text: Behold, I stand here by the well of water; and the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water:

verses.text: And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: let the same be she that thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and thereby shall I know that thou hast shewed kindness unto my master.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Now that was a big ask. Ten camels coming off the desert can drink a whole lot of water. A young woman who offered to water them all was signing up for hours of hard work for a stranger.

verses.text: And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Back and forth from the well to the trough, again and again, till every camel had enough. Nobody asked her to. That was just who she was. Kindness was in her bones.

verses.text: And the man wondering at her held his peace, to wit whether the LORD had made his journey prosperous or not.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The servant just watched her, quiet, waiting to see if this was really God's answer.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Bethuel. Nahor. That was Abraham's own family. Out of every woman in that town, the one who came down to the well was kin to his master.

verses.text: And the man bowed down his head, and worshipped the LORD.

verses.text: And he said, Blessed be the LORD God of my master Abraham, who hath not left destitute my master of his mercy and his truth: I being in the way, the LORD led me to the house of my master’s brethren.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The first thing that servant did was not to celebrate or make a plan. He bowed his head right there by the well and gave God the praise. He said the LORD led him while he was on the way. Church, when you are on the way, doing what you were sent to do, God knows how to lead you right where you need to be.

pastor.note: Faithful to Gen 24:10-27; v16 skipped; the servant's prayer and thanks kept as scripture, v27 echoed in our own words.

cultural.note: 'Before he had done speaking' at the turn; Rebekah's kindness and labour honoured, no romance gloss.
